profile.name: Hamid R. Rezaei
profile.headline: Full-Stack Software Engineer
profile.tagline: I build Java/Spring services, secure APIs, and React interfaces. I enjoy working through data-heavy problems and making software easier to test, release, and support.

timeline.title: What I’ve worked on.
timeline.description: My roles, side projects, and education, with a closer look at the work along the way.

skills.title: Tools I work with.
skills.description: Java and Spring are at the centre of my work. These are the languages, frameworks, and tools I use across the frontend, data, and delivery.

contact.title: Let’s talk.

timeline.title: Full-Stack Engineer
timeline.summary: I build services, analytics, and internal tools for Agency Securities Lending, from secure APIs to React interfaces and AI-assisted workflows.

highlights.title: Secure services and integrations
highlights.body: I develop Java/Spring Boot microservices and REST APIs that integrate with other bank services. I implemented Spring Security and JWT authorization, with JPA for access to a cloud-hosted relational database.

highlights.title: A multi-service platform proof of concept
highlights.body: I co-architected a multi-service proof of concept with an Active Directory authentication service, an API gateway, and a React frontend.
details: Built configuration-driven APIs for datasets with 100+ columns, with filtering and sorting.

metric.label: One selected trade type · defined evaluation period

highlights.title: An assistant inside the product
highlights.body: I designed and built a React and Spring AI assistant that uses active filters, table metadata, and displayed results to answer questions in context.
details: Supported JSON and streamed SSE responses, then extracted components for reuse by other teams.

highlights.title: Helping teams use coding agents
highlights.body: I built shared coding-agent workflows and script-backed skills connecting GitHub, Jira, Confluence, logs, and Jenkins. I helped teams put them to use through hands-on training and knowledge-sharing sessions.

highlights.title: Revenue and balance analytics
highlights.body: I build SQL-based Looker Studio dashboards over BigQuery for revenue and balance analysis, working with product and business users.

highlights.title: Replacing the old release scripts
highlights.body: I led the migration from legacy scripts to Jenkins/Groovy pipelines covering builds, tests, security scans, artifact versioning, and deployments across environments.
details: Integrated Sonatype and Checkmarx security scans, artifact versioning, Jira, and Confluence into the release workflow.

timeline.title: Full-Stack Engineer
timeline.summary: I worked on data synchronization, real-time processing, and internal tools used to support trading systems.

highlights.title: A reusable synchronization product
highlights.body: I owned the architecture, code reviews, and delivery roadmap for a modular Spring Batch product for data transfer and synchronization. New use cases could be configured without duplicating the implementation.

highlights.title: Processing events in the right order
highlights.body: I contributed to a configurable, event-driven ETL application processing real-time trading data with Java 21, Spring Integration, Solace, and PostgreSQL.
details: Implemented acknowledgments, retries, exception handling, and transactional controls to preserve lifecycle-event order and reduce the risk of data loss during concurrent processing.

highlights.title: A secure file-retrieval tool
highlights.body: I designed and owned a production file-retrieval tool using React, Spring Boot, and Spring Security. It guided authorized users to the files they needed while enforcing access controls on the backend.

highlights.title: Seeing what the applications were doing
highlights.body: I built parameterized Grafana dashboards to make application health and performance easier to monitor.

highlights.title: A path off legacy systems
highlights.body: I evaluated existing functionality and designed scalable alternatives that could be introduced through a phased migration.

timeline.title: Software Developer & DevOps Engineer
timeline.summary: I developed regulatory trade-reporting features for the Americas and built the automation used to test and release them.

highlights.title: Regression analysis in three hours
highlights.body: I built a platform that split large datasets across parallel Jenkins pipelines and brought the results together in a multithreaded Spring Boot application. Analysis that had taken a week could be completed in three hours.

highlights.title: Reporting across the Americas
highlights.body: I delivered reporting functionality in Java and Drools for CFTC, SEC, and Canadian regulators.

highlights.title: Build, release, and change management
highlights.body: I created modular Jenkins/Groovy pipelines connecting GitHub, Maven, Nexus, Jira, Ansible, and ServiceNow for build, deployment, and change-management workflows.

highlights.title: Keeping production running
highlights.body: I refactored legacy applications using OOP and SOLID principles and automated production operations with Bash. I also supported L2/L3 incident diagnosis and resolution with an international agile team.

timeline.title: Master of Engineering
timeline.summary: I used mathematical modeling and R to study hydrological and spatial problems, turning domain concepts into equations and statistical analysis.

timeline.title: Computer Science & Mathematics Teacher
timeline.summary: I taught computer science and mathematics at two high schools and through private tutoring. Topics included algorithms, flowcharts, spreadsheets, algebra, and probability.

timeline.title: Bachelor of Science
timeline.summary: I studied civil engineering, with a strong grounding in mathematics and quantitative analysis.

timeline.title: man-agent-ment
timeline.summary: I built an open-source workflow kit for the coding agents I use across projects. It gives them a consistent way to plan changes, check their work, and leave useful context for the next session.

highlights.title: One workflow across coding tools
highlights.body: Built a portable POSIX-shell toolkit with small adapters for Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and GitHub Copilot. Shared workflows, skills, templates, and scripts travel with the project.

metric.label: Versioned workflows, skills, templates, scripts, and adapters

highlights.title: Leaving context for the next session
highlights.body: Standardized planning, project knowledge, and session handoffs. Context-injection hooks keep guidance available, while non-overwriting installation and adoption audits protect existing project files.
details: Added CI smoke tests for the toolkit and its installation workflows.

timeline.title: BuyOrRent
timeline.summary: I’m building financial tools for housing-cost comparisons. The TypeScript backend is live, with HTTP APIs and MCP tools sharing the same calculation logic. The Flutter frontend is in progress.

highlights.title: A shared calculation engine
highlights.body: Built a TypeScript/Hono backend on Cloudflare Workers for rent, loan, mortgage, property, investment, and expense projections. OpenAPI HTTP endpoints and MCP tools share the same financial-domain logic.
details: Used precise decimal arithmetic with explicit rules for accrual, scheduling, and rounding.

highlights.title: Financial tools for AI assistants
highlights.body: Exposed the calculations as MCP tools for AI assistants, with structured results and strict Zod contracts. HTTP and MCP share validation and consistent errors.

highlights.title: Results you can inspect
highlights.body: Added dated cash-flow breakdowns and CSV exports backed by private Cloudflare R2 storage. GitHub Actions handles delivery across DEV, UAT, and PROD.
details: The full buy-versus-rent comparison and Flutter integration are still in progress.

timeline.title: Buildean
timeline.summary: I co-founded Buildean, a construction-estimation platform in beta. I build the backend and cloud infrastructure, from the estimation engine to secure APIs and delivery pipelines.

highlights.title: The backend behind the estimates
highlights.body: I architected a Java 25/Spring Boot 4 backend with PostgreSQL, Flyway migrations, and modular REST services documented through OpenAPI.

highlights.title: Keeping estimates useful as plans change
highlights.body: Built a transaction-safe estimation engine around hierarchical work scopes, quote resolution, and manual price overrides. Scenario copying and bidirectional task–estimate synchronization keep estimates useful as plans change.

highlights.title: A repeatable path to the cloud
highlights.body: Secured APIs with Firebase authentication, role-based access, and ownership controls. Automated keyless GitHub Actions delivery to GCP Cloud Run and Cloud SQL across DEV and UAT.
